newsitem.title: USA: Anadarko says on target for 17 pct output growth.
newsitem.headline: Anadarko says on target for 17 pct output growth.

text.p: Anadarko Petroleum Corp expects to increase crude oil and natural gas production by 17 percent this year, the company said in a statement with earnings.

"The Company's financial performance during the first quarter was outstanding ... but more encouraging are the significant achievements in drilling programs in our core operating areas. Anadarko is on-track to meet our goal of increasing production by 17 percent in 1997," said chief executive Robert Allison.
Net income rose to $34.4 million, $0.58 per share, on revenues of $170.5 million in the first quarter from $20.5 million, $0.35 cents per share, on revenues of $135.7 million a year ago.
Crude oil and condensate volumes were up 18 percent to 2 million barrels per day (mmbd) and 0.2 mmbd, respectively, compared to 1.7 mmbd and 0.19 mmbd a year ago.

The increase in oil production volumes is primarily due to Anadarko's drilling programs in the Permian Basin of west Texas and southwest Kansas, along with initial oil production from the Mahogany platform in the Gulf of Mexico.
The average U.S. oil price was $20.58 per barrel, up from $17.64 a year ago.
Anadarko produced 470 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) compared to 480 mmcfd of natural gas a year ago.
Anadarko Energy Services Co, marketed about 830 mmcfd of third-party gas compared with 527 mmcfd of third-party gas in the same period of 1996.
Average U.S. wellhead gas prices rose 36 percent to $2.66 per thousand cubic feet from $1.96 a year ago.
Natural gas liquids sales increased 25 percent to 14 mmbd per day compared to 11 mmbd per day a year ago.
Prices rose to $15.65 from $14.29 per barrel.
In the first quarter, Anadarko drilled drilled or participated in 126 wells, including 75 oil wells, 40 gas wells and 11 dry holes.
It drilled 61 wells a year ago. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
